text: A Large Language Model, or LLM, is trained on vast amounts of text—books, articles, and websites—learning how language works and ideas connect.
Its core mechanism is simple: given some text, it predicts what text should come next, one small piece at a time.
The model does not read whole words like we do.
It processes tokens—small pieces of text that can be a word, part of a word, or punctuation.
When generating a response, the LLM weighs several likely options and picks one.
Because it chooses among likely options rather than following rigid formulas, asking the same question twice can produce two different, equally reasonable answers.
Always read and judge the output.
